title: shred-audit
description: Per-provider shred delivery. provider_stats and audit_counters hold per-interval DELTAS, so panels aggregate over the selected range rather than reading a running total. Top row is absolute and works with a single provider; the row below it is relative and needs two.

target.rawSql:
SELECT started_at AS time,
       'collector ' || tool_version || ' @ ' || git_commit AS text,
       'restart' AS tags
FROM audit_runs
WHERE host = '$host' AND $__timeFilter(started_at)

list.name: host
list.label: capture host
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT host FROM provider_stats ORDER BY 1
list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT host FROM provider_stats ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Clean set rate — every shred in the set verified
panels.description:
A set counts as clean only when EVERY shred in it verified, none lacked a known leader, and enough arrived to reconstruct it (agg.rs: `invalid == 0 && unverifiable == 0 && decode_ns.is_some()`). Missed shreds do NOT count against it — Reed-Solomon rebuilds a set from any k of k+m.

It is an all-or-nothing gate over ~60 shreds, so it AMPLIFIES a small per-shred failure rate: at 1% per shred barely half the sets come out clean. Never read this as 'half the data is garbage'. Read the per-shred panel beside it first — that is the honest rate, and this one is its 60th power.

No threshold line: we have no baseline yet. Set one once a week of normal traffic says what normal is.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider AS metric,
       sets_valid::float / NULLIF(sets_present, 0) * 100 AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Per-shred failure rates — the honest number
panels.description:
What the previous panel is made of, without the ~60x per-set amplification.

'invalid' is shreds that failed verification, over shreds delivered. 'no leader' is shreds we could not check at all because the slot's leader was unknown — if that is non-zero the invalid rate is understated and the leader schedule is the thing to fix. 'missed' is over shreds EXPECTED (delivered + missed), so it is comparable between providers regardless of how much traffic each carried.

Providers that delivered nothing are excluded on purpose: a silent feed would otherwise draw a flat 0% and read as the cleanest one on the board.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider || ' · invalid' AS metric,
       invalid::float / (shreds_data + shreds_code) * 100 AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
  AND shreds_data + shreds_code > 0
UNION ALL
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider || ' · no leader' AS metric,
       sig_unverifiable::float / (shreds_data + shreds_code) * 100 AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
  AND shreds_data + shreds_code > 0
UNION ALL
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider || ' · missed' AS metric,
       missed::float / (missed + shreds_data + shreds_code) * 100 AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
  AND shreds_data + shreds_code > 0
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Set fill time — how long THIS provider took
panels.description: From a provider's first accepted shred of a set to the one that made the set decodable. The only ABSOLUTE latency here: winrate and 'behind fastest' are relative, so a change that slows every provider equally moves neither of them and moves this one. Needs no second provider. 'worst' is the slowest single set in the interval — an intermittent stall barely shifts the mean and spikes there.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider || ' · mean' AS metric,
       fill_sum_us / NULLIF(fill_n, 0) AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
UNION ALL
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider || ' · worst' AS metric,
       fill_max_us AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Winrate — share of contested FEC sets decoded first
panels.description: A set is contested only when two or more providers delivered it validly; delivering alone is not a win. Ties count as a win for each. Empty with a single provider — see the panel's no-data text.

defaults.noValue: no contested sets in this range — a race needs TWO providers delivering the same FEC set validly. With one provider this is empty by definition, not broken. The absolute panels above still work.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider AS metric,
       wins::float / races * 100 AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
  AND races > 0
ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Winner share per source
panels.description: Share of first-delivery (unique) shreds by source. Sums to 100%.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider AS metric,
       wins::float / NULLIF(sum(wins) over(partition by ts), 0) * 100 AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Behind the fastest provider
panels.description: Microseconds behind whoever decoded each contested set first. Mean is SUM(behind_sum_us)/SUM(behind_n) — the table stores the sum unreduced so any range divides exactly, instead of averaging pre-averaged intervals. Run the old and new forwarder side by side as two providers and this panel is the migration verdict.

defaults.noValue: no contested sets in this range — a race needs TWO providers delivering the same FEC set validly. With one provider this is empty by definition, not broken. The absolute panels above still work.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider || ' · mean' AS metric,
       behind_sum_us / behind_n AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
  AND behind_n > 0
UNION ALL
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider || ' · worst' AS metric,
       behind_max_us AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
  AND behind_n > 0
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Coverage — sets this provider turned up for
panels.description: sets_present / sets_total, where the denominator is every distinct set ANY provider delivered this interval. Presence only, valid or not. With a single provider it is 100% by construction — read it next to the usable set rate at the top, never on its own.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider AS metric,
       sets_present::float / NULLIF(sets_total, 0) * 100 AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
ORDER BY ts

panels.title: FEC sets per second
panels.description: Delivery rate per provider, divided by the row's own window_secs so a short first interval or a stalled loop does not distort it.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider AS metric,
       sets_present / NULLIF(window_secs, 0) AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Missed shreds per second
panels.description: Shreds a provider never delivered for sets it was part of. Check host health below FIRST: datagrams the kernel dropped from our own socket are absent from the data and inflate this for whoever sent them.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider AS metric,
       missed / NULLIF(window_secs, 0) AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Failed verification, and repeats
panels.description: 'bad data' is block content the leader never signed — treat as substitution until proven otherwise. 'bad proof' is the leader's genuine data whose merkle proof does not reconstruct the signed root: authentic content, unusable shred. 'unclassified' means no provider delivered a leader-authenticated copy to compare against, so it could not be split — with ONE provider everything lands here and the other two read zero. 'repeats' is the same shred delivered twice.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time, provider || ' · bad data' AS metric, invalid_data AS value FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
UNION ALL
SELECT ts AS time, provider || ' · bad proof' AS metric, invalid_sig AS value FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
UNION ALL
SELECT ts AS time, provider || ' · unclassified' AS metric, invalid_unknown AS value FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
UNION ALL
SELECT ts AS time, provider || ' · repeats' AS metric, duplicated AS value FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Stream integrity — is the wire format still what we expect
panels.description: Per second. shreds_after_window is the REORDERING canary: shreds arriving for FEC sets already finalized, which is what a forwarder that buffers or reorders produces. malformed / no_merkle_root mean packets are being mangled; wrong_version means a different cluster or shred version is being relayed; unsupported_variant means something arrived this build cannot parse. All four are zero on a healthy feed.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       name AS metric,
       value::float / NULLIF(window_secs, 0) AS value
FROM audit_counters
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
  AND name IN ('shreds_after_window', 'shreds_malformed', 'shreds_wrong_version',
               'shreds_unsupported_variant', 'shreds_no_merkle_root', 'shreds_no_leader')
ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Data vs coding shreds per second
panels.description: A forwarder that stops relaying CODING shreds looks alive on every other counter — sets keep arriving, they just stop being recoverable from partial delivery. Nothing else here separates the two, so watch the ratio, not the absolute level.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider || ' · data' AS metric,
       shreds_data / NULLIF(window_secs, 0) AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
UNION ALL
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider || ' · coding' AS metric,
       shreds_code / NULLIF(window_secs, 0) AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Host health — OUR losses, not a provider's
panels.description: Every series here is this machine failing to keep up, not a provider failing to send. udp_kernel_dropped is our socket queue overflowing (raise net.core.rmem_max); udp_channel_full is verification falling behind. Both make the missed-shreds panel look worse than the network was. Non-zero here invalidates a comparison.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       name AS metric,
       value::float / NULLIF(window_secs, 0) AS value
FROM audit_counters
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
  AND name IN ('udp_kernel_dropped', 'udp_channel_full', 'udp_truncated',
               'udp_no_timestamp', 'udp_unmatched')
ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Throughput
panels.description: Datagrams received, shreds parsed out of them, and shreds that failed signature verification — per second.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       name AS metric,
       value::float / NULLIF(window_secs, 0) AS value
FROM audit_counters
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
  AND name IN ('udp_received', 'shreds_parsed', 'shreds_sig_bad')
ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Provider RTT (ICMP)
panels.description: A GAUGE, re-sampled by the pinger on its own timer — consecutive points can repeat one measurement. A coarse network-distance hint, NOT comparable to the decode deltas: ICMP travels a different path and is routinely deprioritised. Use it to EXPLAIN a latency difference, never to measure one. Null = no reply.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider || ' ' || ip AS metric,
       rtt_ms AS value
FROM provider_pings
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Transaction deliveries per second — when a feed went quiet
panels.description: txn_source_stats is cumulative, so consecutive rows are differenced here to get a rate. A restart resets the counters, which would read as a large negative rate; those points are dropped so the line breaks instead of diving. The table below says a feed fell behind — this says when.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time,
       metric,
       CASE WHEN d >= 0 THEN d / NULLIF(dt, 0) END AS value
FROM (
  SELECT ts     AS time,
         source AS metric,
         seen - LAG(seen) OVER (PARTITION BY source ORDER BY ts) AS d,
         EXTRACT(epoch FROM ts - LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY source ORDER BY ts)) AS dt
  FROM txn_source_stats
  WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
) s
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Transaction sources — CUMULATIVE for the run
panels.description: The one cumulative table: percentiles come from a histogram spanning the whole process, so this is the latest row per source, not an interval, and it resets when the collector restarts. Do not SUM these columns. onchain bad % is a SAMPLED audit against getBlock — compare sources on the percentage, never on raw counts, and remember pre-execution feeds legitimately carry transactions that never landed. missed / corrupted / duplicated are its three components and are NOT interchangeable: never delivering a transaction is a different accusation from delivering it altered, and only the raw counts tell them apart.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (source)
       source,
       kind,
       seen,
       contested,
       winrate * 100        AS "win %",
       behind_p50_us       AS "p50 µs",
       behind_p90_us       AS "p90 µs",
       behind_p99_us       AS "p99 µs",
       onchain_missed      AS "missed",
       onchain_corrupted   AS "corrupted",
       onchain_duplicated  AS "duplicated",
       onchain_bad_pct * 100 AS "onchain bad %"
FROM txn_source_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
ORDER BY source, ts DESC
